name: replies-are-not-in-time-order
rule: A thread is assembled from several Graph calls, so its replies are NOT chronological. 'Who spoke last' must be answered from the clock, never from array position.
why: T-36, 2026-09-14. activity.ts flattened a thread as [...second-level, ...third-level] and triage read replies.at(-1). Identical only while the thread has ONE branch. With two, the Page's older answer on branch A sorts behind a visitor's newer comment on branch B, and the thread reports `answered` with a customer waiting — T-11's inversion, in T-11's direction, inside the code T-11's fix was written into. Found by computing the answer a second way, from timestamps, before the probe ever reached Graph. Mutation-checking this case found that it did not, at first, catch the mutation it was written for: T-36 was fixed in TWO places — the assembler sorts what it builds and the triage answers from timestamps — so breaking either alone leaves the other covering, and only breaking BOTH (which is what a port written from the README would do) failed the case. The verdict assertion therefore tests the composite property. The ordering assertion below was added so the case can also disagree with the assembler alone.

data.message: Second: still waiting on this one.
